title: Spiced apple and prune compote with walnuts

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Apples, prunes, an orange, walnuts, Greek yoghurt, honey and cinnamon are all plain cupboard and fridge foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded saucepan, a frying pan, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple simmering and toasting.

works.reason: Six eating apples with 100g prunes, orange juice and 100ml water simmered covered for 10 to 12 minutes gives a soft compote that holds its shape, enough to top 500g yoghurt for four.

honest_times.reason: Coring six apples, halving prunes, zesting and juicing an orange and toasting walnuts fits in 15 minutes, and the 12-minute simmer matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, nothing unlisted apart from water is used, and each name matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm spiced apple compote suits a cold late-December morning, and the apples are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, Greek yoghurt and walnuts with only a spoonful of honey make a proper, satisfying breakfast a family would eat again.
